name: PixiTween Director S23: sheet film (every product film 3D, checked on product, element, set and film sheets)
description: Every new product film is made as one 3D film: Muse's board (with lock lines and the asked length), then product, element and set sheets rendered by our own engine and checked in one Muse look, then the film built from JSON, checked by code rules, shown as a film sheet and looked at once, then committed. The 2D crew no longer runs for a new film (FILM_PATH=crew keeps it until a later PRD deletes it). Leaves out: deleting the 2D crew code, an approval gate, chat edits of a 3D film.

userStories.title: Board lock lines
userStories.description: As a writer of the board (Muse), I want to write two to four lock lines on the board so that the sheets and the film sheet are checked against what must stay true in every shot.
steps: Read server/authoring/beatsheet.ts: CinematicBoard, the board zod schema used by parseBoard, the JSON template line and the prompt paragraphs in boardPrompt, and server/authoring/beatsheet.test.ts (parseBoard and planBoard tests).

Add `locks?: string[]` to CinematicBoard and to the schema: at most 4 strings, each 8 to 120 characters, trimmed; a reply with more keeps the first 4; a bad value is dropped (use .catch(undefined) like the other optional fields), never a refusal of the board.

Add `"locks?":["what must stay true in every shot"]` to the JSON template in boardPrompt, and one paragraph: LOCKS are 2 to 4 short lines about the product and the world that must hold in every shot (its colours, its label facing, what the elements are), checked on the sheets and the film.
Carry locks through parseBoard and reviewBoard unchanged; a revised board from planBoard with prior keeps its own locks.
Add tests: locks parsed from a reply; 6 locks kept as 4; a 300-character lock dropped; the prompt contains the LOCKS paragraph.
acceptanceCriteria: parseBoard of a board with locks ['the tub is white with a pink label'] returns board.locks equal to that array
parseBoard with 6 valid locks returns 4, and with a lock of 300 characters returns no such lock and ok true
boardPrompt({ title: 'X', seconds: 8 }).system contains the word LOCKS

userStories.title: Asked length from the brief, and a storyboard from the board
userStories.description: As a step of the sheet film, I want the length the brief asks for and a storyboard made from Muse's board so that the plan panel shows the shots of a 3D film.
steps: Read shared/storyboard.ts (sceneSchema: durationSec 2 to 8, shotType, camera, layersWanted, mode, modeReason; storyboardSchema) and the Beat type and PHASES in server/authoring/beatsheet.ts.

Create server/crew/sheet-film/plan.ts exporting secondsIn(text: string): number | undefined: the first '<n>s', '<n> s', '<n> sec', '<n> seconds' in the text, 4 to 20 inclusive, else undefined; and askedSeconds(text) = Math.min(10, secondsIn(text) ?? 8).

In the same file export storyboardFromBoard(board: CinematicBoard, o: { title: string; aspect: Aspect }): Storyboard: consecutive beats grouped into scenes of at least 2 s and at most 8 s (a short last group joins the one before), scene ids shot-1, shot-2, ...; intent from the beats' notes or words (1 to 300 chars); text from the first beat with words; shotType from phase (hook hero, build detail, peak lifestyle, reveal reveal, close closer, none detail); camera from the first beat's move (push/pull/dolly-zoom dolly-in, orbit orbit, truck pan, crane parallax, hold/whip/rack static); layersWanted ['bg','product']; mode '3d'; modeReason 'one 3D film'.
The storyboard's durationSec is the board's total rounded to 0.1 s, and it parses with storyboardSchema.

Create server/crew/sheet-film/plan.test.ts with the yoghurt case: 'Cinematic 10s vertical (9:16) yoghurt ad' gives 10; 'a 6 second film' gives 6; 'version 2' gives undefined; a board of beats 1.2, 2, 1.8, 2.3, 2.7 s gives scenes whose durations are each 2 to 8 and sum to 10.
acceptanceCriteria: secondsIn('Cinematic 10s vertical (9:16) yoghurt ad') returns 10 and secondsIn('a 6 second film') returns 6
askedSeconds('no length given') returns 8 and askedSeconds('a 15s film') returns 10
storyboardFromBoard of beats [1.2, 2, 1.8, 2.3, 2.7] returns scenes that each last 2 to 8 s, sum to 10 s, have mode '3d', and pass storyboardSchema.parse

userStories.title: Product sheet composition: the 3D product turned four ways
userStories.description: As a sheet check, I want a small composition that shows the real 3D product front, three-quarter, side and back under neutral light so that a wrong cut-out or a wrong colour shows before the film is built.
steps: Read server/authoring/cinematic-film.ts (how buildCinematicFilm makes the cine:world stage3d layer and the cine:product prop from CinematicInput), shared/aep/stage3d.ts and shared/aep/layer.ts (stage3d and prop3d), and server/engine/light-validator.ts.

Create server/crew/sheet-film/sheets.ts exporting productSheetComp(film: Comp): Comp | undefined. It takes the built film, copies its cine:product prop (and the assets that prop uses) into a new composition of 4 frames at 1 fps, aspect 1:1 (1080 x 1080).

The new composition has one stage3d world with the studio lights preset, a neutral grey backdrop (no set, no ground colour from the board, no post grade, exposure 1), a fixed camera framing the product at fill about 0.6, and the product's rotation as hold keys: frame 0 yaw 0, frame 1 yaw 45, frame 2 yaw 90, frame 3 yaw 180.
Return undefined when the film has no cine:product prop.

Create server/crew/sheet-film/sheets.test.ts: build a film with buildCinematicFilm as server/authoring/cinematic-film.test.ts does, then check productSheetComp's frames, the four yaw keys, that it has no grade and that lightValidate accepts it.
acceptanceCriteria: productSheetComp(film) returns a composition with durationInFrames 4 and width equal to height
the product prop's rotation keys at frames 0, 1, 2, 3 have yaw 0, 45, 90 and 180 with hold true
lightValidate(productSheetComp(film)) returns ok true, and productSheetComp of a film without cine:product returns undefined

userStories.title: Element and set sheet compositions
userStories.description: As a sheet check, I want each element shown alone and the empty set shown under the board's light so that a wrong element or a wrong grade shows before the film is built.
steps: Read server/crew/sheet-film/sheets.ts (US-003) and, in server/authoring/cinematic-film.ts, how element props (ids cine:ing<n>-<kind>) and the set (backdrop, ground, set fields of the world) are made.

Add elementSheetComp(film: Comp): Comp | undefined to sheets.ts: one frame per element prop of the film (at most 6), each frame showing only that element centred on the neutral studio world of US-003, with its own material and textures; undefined when the film has no element props.

Add setSheetComp(film: Comp): Comp: 2 frames; the film's own world (its set, lights, post grade, exposure) with every prop hidden (opacity 0 or removed); frame 0 a wide view from the front, frame 1 the reverse view (camera turned 180 degrees round the world's target).

Export sheetLabels(film: Comp): { product: string[]; elements: string[]; set: string[] } with the panel labels: 'front', '3/4', 'side', 'back'; each element's id and action from the board notes in the film (fall back to the id); 'wide', 'reverse'.

Extend sheets.test.ts: a film with two elements gives a 2-frame element sheet whose frames each hold one element; the set sheet has 2 frames, keeps the world's post grade and has no visible prop; lightValidate accepts both.
acceptanceCriteria: elementSheetComp of a film with elements raspberry and honey returns a composition with durationInFrames 2, and each frame shows exactly one element prop
setSheetComp(film) has durationInFrames 2, keeps the film world's post grade, and no prop is visible in it

userStories.title: Sheet image composer with labels and colour swatches

swatchesOf of a picture half #ff0000 and half #0000ff returns two colours within 0.05 of red and blue

steps: Read shared/composition.ts and shared/events.ts (the asset role union and the art.asset event), server/crew/cinematic-cut.ts (how ctx.assets.put and ctx.emit art.asset are used) and server/crew/sheet-film/sheets.ts and compose.ts.

Create server/crew/sheet-film/render.ts exporting drawSheets(ctx: ToolCtx, o: { film: Comp; photo: Buffer; render: (comp: Comp, times: number[]) => Promise<Buffer[]> }): Promise<PartSheets> where PartSheets = { product?: Buffer; elements?: Buffer; set?: Buffer; assetIds: string[] }.

userStories.title: Sheet check: one Muse look at the part sheets
userStories.description: As a writer of the board (Muse), I want to see the product, element and set sheets beside the photo and my board so that I can say what is wrong before the film is built.
steps: Read server/crew/frame-review.ts (critiquePrompt, parseCritique and how reviewFrames calls ctx.meta.spark.reviewImages and the ledger) and server/crew/sheet-film/render.ts.

Create server/crew/sheet-film/check.ts exporting sheetCheckPrompt(o: { board: CinematicBoard; title: string; sheets: string[] }): string. It says: the first picture is the real photo, then the sheets in order (named); asks whether the 3D product matches the photo (shape, label, colours), whether each element is what the board names, whether the set reads as the board's look and light, and whether the lock lines hold; asks for JSON {"fine": boolean, "problems": [string], "dropElements": [element id]}.

Export parseSheetCheck(raw: unknown, elementIds: string[]): { fine: boolean; problems: string[]; dropElements: string[] }: problems trimmed, at most 6, each at most 300 characters; dropElements only ids in elementIds; an unreadable reply gives { fine: true, problems: [], dropElements: [] }, because the check never blocks a film.

Export checkSheets(ctx: ToolCtx, o: { photo: Buffer; sheets: PartSheets; board: CinematicBoard; title: string }): one reviewImages call with [photo, ...sheets present], the ledger gets one line of 0.005 USD.

Create server/crew/sheet-film/check.test.ts with a fake spark: a reply naming 'raspberry' in dropElements and an unknown id keeps only raspberry; a non-JSON reply gives fine true; the prompt contains the lock lines and the element ids.
acceptanceCriteria: parseSheetCheck({ fine: false, problems: ['tub is brown'], dropElements: ['raspberry', 'ghost'] }, ['raspberry', 'honey']) returns dropElements ['raspberry'] and problems ['tub is brown']
parseSheetCheck('not json', []) returns fine true with empty problems
checkSheets makes exactly one reviewImages call whose images are the photo followed by the sheets present, and adds one ledger entry

userStories.title: JSON rules on the built film (no render)
userStories.description: As a step of the sheet film, I want code rules on the film's JSON so that a wrong length, a covered product or words off the frame are caught before anything is rendered.
steps: Read scripts/titles-harness.ts (the CHECKS block: words inside the frame, no two lines on top of each other, the prop limit), server/authoring/titles3d.ts (titleSpace, wordsBox, TITLE_PROPS_MAX), server/engine/light-validator.ts and server/authoring/beatsheet.ts (totalSeconds, LENGTH_SLACK).
Create server/crew/sheet-film/json-rules.ts exporting jsonRules(film: Comp, o: { askedSeconds: number; aspect: Aspect }): string[]: problems in words for Muse, empty when the film passes.

Rules: lightValidate fails (name its first issue); the length differs from askedSeconds by more than LENGTH_SLACK; a stage world has more than TITLE_PROPS_MAX props; a title is outside the frame (3 % margin); two titles overlap while both are on screen for more than 0.1 s; a title's box covers more than 35 % of the product's screen box at the middle of a shot (estimate the product's screen box from the camera fill of that shot, centred, as cinematic-film.ts frames it).
Move the title box helpers the harness uses into json-rules.ts and import them back into scripts/titles-harness.ts so both share one implementation; the harness output stays the same.

Create server/crew/sheet-film/json-rules.test.ts: a film built for 10 s with askedSeconds 8 gives a length problem; a film with a title moved off the frame gives an outside problem; a clean film gives [].
acceptanceCriteria: jsonRules of a 10 s film with askedSeconds 8 returns a problem that contains '10' and '8'
jsonRules of a film whose title is moved to x beyond the frame returns a problem that names the title's words
jsonRules of the clean film built in the test returns an empty array, and `npx tsx scripts/titles-harness.ts --board <a saved board>` still prints its CHECKS section

userStories.title: Film sheet and one Muse look with at most one revision
userStories.description: As a writer of the board (Muse), I want the whole film as one labelled sheet with what the code measured so that I can fix it once before it ships.
steps: Read server/crew/frame-review.ts (keyTimes, measureFrames, critiquePrompt, parseCritique, reviewFrames and its second revision), server/crew/sheet-film/compose.ts and json-rules.ts, and planBoard's prior option in server/authoring/beatsheet.ts.

Create server/crew/sheet-film/film-sheet.ts exporting filmSheetTimes(board): the middle of each beat and the last frame of the last beat; and filmSheetLabels(board): '[0.0-1.2s] wide push, hard cut' style, with the beat's words in quotes when it has some.

Export lookAtFilm(ctx, o: { board; title; brief; photo?; askedSeconds; build: (b: CinematicBoard) => Comp; render; jsonProblems: (c: Comp) => string[]; log }): Promise<{ board; film: Comp; sheet: Buffer; revised: boolean; problems: string[] }>.

lookAtFilm builds the film, renders the film sheet frames, composes the film sheet, measures the frames (measureFrames), adds jsonProblems, and makes one reviewImages call with [photo, sheet] and a prompt that lists the board's shots, its lock lines and the measured and rule problems.

When Muse or the code names problems, planBoard is called once with prior { board, violations: problems } and the same seconds; a muse board is kept with the board's elements and set, the film is rebuilt and the film sheet drawn again (no second look, no second revision). A floor board or a failed call keeps the first board.
Save the final film sheet with ctx.assets.put role 'sheet' and emit art.asset. Log one line per step with its seconds.

Create server/crew/sheet-film/film-sheet.test.ts with fake spark, render and build: a clean look makes no planBoard call; a look naming a problem makes exactly one planBoard call and returns revised true; the labels of a 3-beat board are three strings starting with '[0.0-'.
acceptanceCriteria: filmSheetTimes of beats 1, 2, 3 s returns [0.5, 2, 5.97] within 0.05 s
lookAtFilm with a fake Muse reply naming one problem calls planBoard once and returns revised true; with a fine reply it calls planBoard zero times
lookAtFilm saves exactly one asset with role 'sheet' per call

userStories.title: makeSheetFilm: the whole 3D film from brief to commit
userStories.description: As a director app, I want one function that makes a product film as a 3D sheet film so that a new film needs no 2D crew.
steps: Read server/crew/cinematic-cut.ts (prepareParts, the build closure inside cinematicCut, commitCuts usage) and every server/crew/sheet-film/ module.

In server/crew/cinematic-cut.ts export prepareCinematicParts(ctx, log, o?: { seconds?: number }) (prepareParts, using o.seconds when given instead of the storyboard's length) and buildCinematic(ctx, parts, board): Comp (the build closure as a function). Additive: cinematicCut keeps its behaviour and its tests.
Create server/crew/sheet-film/index.ts exporting makeSheetFilm(ctx, o: { log; render?; now? }): Promise<{ ok: true; seconds: Record<string, number> } | { ok: false; reason: string }>.

Steps in order: askedSeconds(brief); parts (no photo or no cut-out: ok false with the reason); if Muse chose a flat 2D film (choosesFlat) build it in 3D anyway and log it; drawSheets; checkSheets; drop the elements Muse named; if the check named problems, one planBoard with prior; lookAtFilm; jsonRules on the final film logged as accepted problems if any remain.

Then commitCuts with only the solid film (keep '3d'); write the storyboard (storyboardFromBoard) with ctx.films.update; return ok true and the seconds each step took (parts, sheets, check, revise, look, commit).
render defaults to renderKeyFrames; now defaults to Date.now (tests pass a fake clock).

Create server/crew/sheet-film/index.test.ts with every dependency faked through vi.mock of the sheet-film modules and cinematic-cut: the happy path commits one version and writes a storyboard; parts undefined returns ok false with a reason; a sheet check with problems leads to exactly one planBoard call.
acceptanceCriteria: makeSheetFilm on the happy path returns ok true and calls commitCuts once with no flat cut and keep '3d'
makeSheetFilm when prepareCinematicParts returns undefined returns ok false with a reason that mentions the photo or the cut-out
the returned seconds has the keys parts, sheets, check, look and commit, and cinematicCut's existing tests still pass

userStories.title: New films take the sheet film path; no 2D crew, no stray timer

Add FILM_PATH to server/env.ts: '3d' (default) or 'crew'.

In start(), for a new film (not resume, not the fake director, CINEMATIC_CUT not '0') with FILM_PATH '3d': set status planning, say 'Making the 3D film: plan, sheets, film sheet', set status building, await makeSheetFilm(toolCtx, { log }) and then set status ready (ok) or failed with an error event naming the reason (not ok). Do not start the showrunner, do not call startCinematic, and end the session so the finally block clears the wrap timer.
With FILM_PATH 'crew' the old path runs unchanged.
Log the seconds makeSheetFilm returned as one showrunner.say note ('parts 52 s, sheets 21 s, ...').

Add a test in server/crew/run-crew.test.ts (or a new server/crew/sheet-film/run.test.ts if run-crew.test.ts does not exist) with makeSheetFilm mocked: a new film ends ready with no showrunner model call; a failed sheet film ends failed with an error event; FILM_PATH=crew calls the showrunner.
acceptanceCriteria: a new film with makeSheetFilm mocked to ok true emits film.status planning, building and ready in that order and the showrunner backend is never called
a new film with makeSheetFilm mocked to ok false ends with status failed and an error event that contains the reason
with FILM_PATH=crew the showrunner backend is called, as before

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.
For engine behaviour (composition JSON, Player, timeline, layer kinds) read docs/engine/README.md before writing code; never edit or copy engine source.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.

Before the first story: confirm server/crew/backdrop.ts, server/authoring/titles3d.ts and the export quotedName in server/crew/cinematic-cut.ts exist. If any is missing the branch lacks the owner's 4 Nov work: set notes to 'blocked: base branch lacks the 4 Nov work' and stop.

Run this PRD in its own git worktree (ralph/README.md section 3). Never edit files in the owner's main checkout: its dev server (tsx watch on port 8787) restarts on any server/ edit and kills a film that is building.

`npm test` has 6 known failures outside your files: server/agent/director.test.ts (1), server/http/app.test.ts (1), server/http/middleware.chain.test.ts (2), server/http/handlers/exports.test.ts (1), server/http/handlers/local.test.ts (1). Do not edit those files. The gate passes when no other test fails.
Every Muse call in code goes through ctx.meta.spark (chat or reviewImages) and is added to ctx.ledger like planBoard does. Tests fake ctx.meta.spark; nothing calls the network.

Creative choices stay with Muse (the board, the look, what to revise). Code draws the sheets, measures, checks rules and passes problems back to Muse as words; it never rewrites the board itself except to drop an element Muse named.

Renders in tests are faked: inject the render function (the shape of renderKeyFrames: (composition, times) => Promise<Buffer[]>) and return small sharp-made PNGs. Never launch Chromium in a unit test.
